findings.body: Although the new runtime schema correctly discriminates paging failures, the standard HTTP `ErrorPayload` still uses one object whose `reason`, `fieldErrors`, and `pinnedContinuationLimit` are all optional. Consequently `{ reason: "invalid_pagination" }` and `{ reason: "page_size_changed" }` still type-check through the envelope that the transaction-page endpoint will use. Define the financial-chat branch of this shared type as the discriminated details union so the mandated metadata cannot be omitted.
findings.title: Not done: paging reasons remain optional in the standard error type

findings.body: The required test exercises a valid `FinancialTotal`, but `FinancialComparison` and `ClarificationCard` never appear anywhere in the test file. The suite would therefore still pass if either component rejected every valid payload or stopped enforcing strict props. Add accepted and unknown-prop rejection cases for those component/response branches so all advertised UI contracts are protected.
findings.title: Not done: strict output/UI props

findings.body: The test claims to explain every unavailable state, but only `access_denied` is parsed as a valid unavailable capability. `feature_disabled` is tested only in an intentionally inconsistent enabled fixture, while `no_plant_access` and capability-level `model_unavailable` are never exercised. Removing or breaking any of those required states would leave the suite green; add valid fixtures for every unavailable reason.
findings.title: Not done: capabilities

findings.body: The missing-detail check reads `details[handle]` instead of checking an own property. Because the identifier schema permits names such as `toString`, an advertised Actual with that handle and an empty details record is treated as prepared via `Object.prototype.toString`, so the response can pass without any detail outcome. The analogous result lookup can dereference an inherited function and throw during validation. Use `Object.hasOwn` or null-prototype maps and add reserved-property regression cases.
findings.title: Use own-property checks for result and detail dictionaries

findings.body: This branch defines only the clarification presentation shape; it does not implement pending-request continuation, scope retention, capacity/expiry, revocation checks, cancellation, or restart outcomes required by done-when item 3. The approved task table assigns those behaviors and their end-to-end proofs to MEMORY, GRAPH, API, STREAM, CLIENT, and REGRESSION.
findings.title: Later: MEMORY/GRAPH/API/STREAM/CLIENT/REGRESSION must prove clarification lifecycle

findings.body: The ready/failed detail union is only the presentation contract. Preparation deadlines, source/mapping pins, stable full traversal, authorization rechecks, and browser identity/total comparisons required by done-when item 4 depend on the assigned DRILL, PAGES, ANSWER, DETAIL, and BROWSER tasks.
findings.title: Later: DRILL/PAGES/ANSWER/DETAIL/BROWSER must implement prepared Actual paging

findings.body: Pinning the provider and model ID in capabilities does not establish direct ChatAnthropic execution, trusted instruction ordering, static-prefix caching, payload exclusions, vendor errors, or gated live runs required by done-when item 6. Those implementations and proofs are assigned to MODEL, GRAPH, ANSWER, and LIVE.
findings.title: Later: MODEL/GRAPH/ANSWER/LIVE must prove Claude and static-cache boundaries
